On-Chain Operator. Module 12 · Your own bank. Navy and cyan. This is the door, not the whole module. Education only.
You already keep a journal and a kill rule. A balance sheet is that habit turned into accounts.

By the end of the module you will be able to do this: run your crypto the way a bank runs its book: a balance sheet, a custody policy, a credit line, a liquidity ladder, a lending desk and records someone else could follow. Not before. The lessons earn it one page at a time.

The lessons, in order, are 12.0 Mastery Starter, 12.1 Your balance sheet, 12.2 Custody architecture: vault, multisig and spending policies, 12.3 The credit line: borrowing like a bank client, 12.4 Treasury and the liquidity ladder, 12.5 Being the lender: supplying, curating and pricing credit risk, 12.6 Books, records and succession, 12.7 Tax, regulation and compliance awareness, 12.8 Institutional-grade custody: MPC, custodians and policy engines. You do not skip ahead. Each page is the input to the next.
Lesson 12.0, Mastery Starter. Mastery Starter. You will write that down when you get there.
Lesson 12.1, Your balance sheet. Build a personal on-chain balance sheet and read the three numbers that matter: equity, LTV and liquidity runway. You will write that down when you get there.

Lesson 12.2, Custody architecture: vault, multisig and spending policies. Design custody so that no single lost device, stolen key or mistaken signature can drain the bank. You will write that down when you get there.
Lesson 12.3, The credit line: borrowing like a bank client. Use your assets as collateral for liquidity without selling, under a written credit policy. You will write that down when you get there.
Lesson 12.4, Treasury and the liquidity ladder. Structure reserves so money is available when it's needed, earning a return at every tier. You will write that down when you get there.

Lesson 12.5, Being the lender: supplying, curating and pricing credit risk. Act as the lending side of the bank: choose markets, price the risk, and know when to pull liquidity. You will write that down when you get there.
Lesson 12.6, Books, records and succession. Keep books a stranger could follow, and make sure your family could recover everything if you couldn't. You will write that down when you get there.

Lesson 12.7, Tax, regulation and compliance awareness. Know which on-chain actions may have tax or legal consequences, keep the records to handle them, and know when to get professional help. You will write that down when you get there.

Lesson 12.8, Institutional-grade custody: MPC, custodians and policy engines. Know the custody options institutions use, and when they make sense for a large personal or family book. You will write that down when you get there.
Next is Lesson 12.0, Mastery Starter. Bring nothing but the habit: one idea, one drawing, the word Example on any number. Education only, not financial advice.
